# 1 Chronicles Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 379r–379v

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** And they brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God. **2** When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD. **3** Then he distributed to every person in Israel — both men and women — to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.

**4** Then he appointed some of the Levites as ministers before the ark of the LORD, to invoke, to thank, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.

**5** Asaph was the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with lyres and harps; and Asaph with cymbals sounding aloud; **6** and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.

**7** Then on that day David first appointed Asaph and his brothers to give thanks to the LORD:

**8** Oh give thanks to the LORD; call upon his name;
make known his deeds among the peoples!
**9** Sing to him, sing praises to him;
tell of all his wondrous works!
**10** Glory in his holy name;
let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice!
**11** Seek the LORD and his strength;
seek his presence continually!

**12** Remember the wondrous works that he has done,
his signs and the judgments he uttered,
**13** O offspring of Israel his servant,
sons of Jacob, his chosen ones!
**14** He is the LORD our God;
his judgments are in all the earth.

**15** Remember his covenant forever,
the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
**16** the covenant that he made with Abraham,
his sworn promise to Isaac,
**17** which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
**18** saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan
as your portion of inheritance."

**19** When you were few in number,
of little account, and sojourners in it,
**20** wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people,
**21** he allowed no one to oppress them;
he rebuked kings on their account,
**22** saying, "Touch not my anointed ones,
do my prophets no harm!"

**23** Sing to the LORD, all the earth!
Tell of his salvation from day to day!
**24** Declare his glory among the nations,
his marvelous works among all the peoples!

**25** For great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised,
and he is to be feared above all gods.
**26** For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but the LORD made the heavens.
**27** Splendor and majesty are before him;
strength and joy are in his place.

**28** Ascribe to the LORD, O families of the peoples,
ascribe to the LORD glory and strength!
**29** Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name;
bring an offering and come before him!
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness;
**30** tremble before him, all the earth;
yes, the world is established; it shall never be moved.

**31** Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice,
and let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!"
**32** Let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
let the field exult, and everything in it!
**33** Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy
before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.

**34** Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good;
for his steadfast love endures forever!

**35** Say also: "Save us, O God of our salvation,
and gather and deliver us from among the nations,
that we may give thanks to your holy name
and glory in your praise."

**36** Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!
Then all the people said, "Amen!" and praised the LORD.

**37** So David left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD to minister before the ark regularly, as each day required, **38** along with Obed-edom and his sixty-eight brothers. Obed-edom the son of Jeduthun, and Hosah, were to be gatekeepers.

**39** And he left Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place that was at Gibeon, **40** to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the Law of the LORD that he commanded Israel.

**41** With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and expressly named to give thanks to the LORD, for his steadfast love endures forever. **42** Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for sounding aloud, and instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were appointed to the gate.

**43** Then all the people departed, each to his house, and David went home to bless his household.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This is the theological center of the Chronicler's David narrative. The ark has arrived; the worship is established; the psalm is sung. The Chronicler constructs David's inaugural liturgy from three canonical psalms (105, 96, 106), creating a composite that moves from thanksgiving (vv.8-22) to cosmic praise (vv.23-33) to eschatological petition (vv.34-36). The theological structure is deliberate: remember God's covenant faithfulness (past), declare God's kingship over all creation (present), and pray for God's saving action (future). The modification of Psalm 96:6 in v.27 — "joy" replacing "beauty," "his place" replacing "his sanctuary" — is one of the Chronicler's most revealing editorial changes, acknowledging that the temple does not yet exist while insisting that God's presence is already located. The dual worship arrangement (vv.37-42) — Asaph at the ark in Jerusalem, Zadok at the tabernacle in Gibeon — is the Chronicler's solution to a historical problem: how to legitimize both the Davidic tent and the Mosaic tabernacle before Solomon's temple unifies them. The chapter ends with the simplest of human acts: David goes home to bless his family (v.43).

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "peace offerings" vs. "fellowship offerings"
- **EMET:** "peace-offerings [shelamim]"
- **LOGOS:** "peace offerings"
- **PNEUMA:** "fellowship offerings"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "peace offerings" — *shelamim* derives from *shalom*. While "fellowship offerings" captures the communal meal aspect, "peace offerings" is the traditional rendering and preserves the *shalom* connection.

### V.4 — "invoke" vs. "petition"
- **EMET:** "to-invoke [le-hazkir]"
- **LOGOS:** "to invoke"
- **PNEUMA:** "to petition"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to invoke" — the hiphil of *zakar* means "to cause to remember/invoke," not "to petition." It refers to invoking God's name in worship, not making requests.

### V.26 — "idols" vs. "worthless idols"
- **EMET:** "idols [elilim]"
- **LOGOS:** "idols"
- **PNEUMA:** "worthless idols"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "idols" — while *elilim* does carry connotations of worthlessness (as a pun on *elohim*), the English word "idols" already carries negative weight. PNEUMA's "worthless" is redundant.

### V.31 — "The LORD reigns" vs. "The LORD is king"
- **EMET:** "YHWH reigns [malakh]"
- **LOGOS:** "The LORD reigns"
- **PNEUMA:** "The LORD is king"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "The LORD reigns" — the Hebrew *YHWH malakh* is a verbal clause (he has become king / he reigns), not a nominal predication (he is king). The verbal rendering preserves the dynamic, enthronement-language quality.

### V.33 — "judge" vs. "govern"
- **EMET:** "to-judge [lishpot] the-earth"
- **LOGOS:** "to judge the earth"
- **PNEUMA:** "to govern the earth"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to judge the earth" — the Hebrew *shaphat* encompasses judging, ruling, and setting things right. "Judge" preserves the traditional psalm language and the eschatological dimension.

### V.34 — "steadfast love" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET:** "his-steadfast-love [chasdo]"
- **LOGOS:** "his steadfast love"
- **PNEUMA:** "his faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "his steadfast love" — *chesed* is one of the most theologically weighty words in the Hebrew Bible. "Steadfast love" has become the standard scholarly rendering, capturing both the loyalty and the affection dimensions. PNEUMA's "faithful love" is acceptable but less established.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
